project.purpose: Represent divergent Git history as read-only source-cut-bound typed LEGO records; never infer semantic consumer acceptance or authorize main reset/branch deletion.

nodes.label: SourceHistoryGraphProjection
nodes.responsibility: Project exact local/remote Git commit DAG, patch relation, canonical owner mapping and path evidence, including merge deltas distinct from all parents.
nodes.authority: Git object graph and existing tools/repo/owners.toml
acceptance: Every represented commit binds immutable left/right SourceCut identities and one canonical natural Owner projection, or the operator fails closed.
Independent merge-result path changes remain visible and consumerQualification is UNKNOWN_REQUIRES_OWNER_CDC without separate Owner contract proof.
The existing native test_source_history_legos.py and repository CI pass on the candidate source cut.
Identical unique cross-path Git Blob/mode matches are represented without asserting historical rename intent, path consumer equivalence or automatic deletion; duplicates remain ambiguous.

Retired document currentness, one-off first-contact evaluators and historical live-view tools are not source-of-truth; existing architecture checker remains and a negative CDC rejects their reintroduction.

ROOT_UNOWNED means no matching path in the protected SourceCut Owner manifest, not an inferred root Owner. For those paths the graph partitions exact local/remote tip presence into BOTH_PRESENT, LOCAL_ONLY, REMOTE_ONLY and BOTH_ABSENT; none establishes consumer equivalence or branch-retirement permission.
nodes.nextAction: Per-Owner Consumer-Driven Contract qualification of surviving divergent histories; no redundant Git scanner.

nodes.label: CanonicalOwnerAndSourceCutGate
nodes.responsibility: Reject unknown natural owner identities, redirected source inputs or forged owner plans using the existing repository checker and canonical owners.toml.
nodes.authority: tools/repo/owners.toml, Git SourceCut tree and tools/repo/check_architecture_docs.py
acceptance: An issue with an undeclared or prefix-spoofed naturalOwner is rejected under exact canonical owners.toml.
A symlink-redirected owner plan, census input or owner manifest is rejected before it can impersonate the source-owned artifact.
The existing repo architecture tests and check_architecture_docs.py pass without a new owner discovery mechanism.
Typed LEGO slice blockers must form a well-founded prerequisite DAG; self-cycles and mutual deadlocks fail the current Owner source-bound graph gate.
Every BLOCKED_ON prerequisite is currently unresolved; a partly completed blocker set is invalid even when another predecessor remains open.
nodes.nextAction: Reuse existing native source-bound validator; no duplicate graph, custom DSL, or new proof runtime.

slices.label: DivergentMainSourceHistory
acceptance: Native Git projection covers both exclusive DAG sides and refuses ambiguous common ancestors rather than selecting arbitrary lineage.
Projected equality may skip redundant cherry-picks for exact source paths, never approve deletion or imply behavior equality.
Owner-native test_source_history_legos.py validates NUL-delimited paths, merge paths, source-bound owners and fail-closed edges.
blockers: Consumer semantic equivalence remains UNKNOWN until corresponding natural-Owner CDC is proven.
slices.nextAction: Select and test only novel consumer behavior in recorded Git cuts.

slices.label: NaturalOwnerMembership
acceptance: TYPE-01 binds its actual consumer to a declared owners.toml root or tools/repo; undeclared and prefix-impersonator owners fail the native contract.
The canonical Owner list remains the only classification source; no new validation registry or account-specific owner system.
Self and mutual BLOCKED_ON prerequisite cycles are rejected via existing graphlib.TopologicalSorter; non-prerequisite feedback remains legal.
Every BLOCKED_ON prerequisite is currently unresolved; a partly completed blocker set is invalid even when another predecessor remains open.

The read-only Git publication source-cut gate accepts only a native object-format-qualified remote OID (40 SHA-1, 64 SHA-256), distinguishes cached tracking from live remote, and never treats matching local/tracking refs alone as publication proof.

A primary-main source certificate must reject tracked Git index concealment flags (assume-unchanged/skip-worktree) even if native diff, status, and index-tree equality appear clean; a concealed-byte source is not an eligible Git publication witness.

Every registered Owner planning slice uses a recognized finite lifecycle status or a fully qualified BLOCKED_ON_* prerequisite expression; unknown/typo states are rejected at the existing native architecture admission gate, including slices with no census consumer.

Game and Media active Owner LEGO planning graphs are admitted through the existing repository-native node/edge/type and graphlib dependency verification on every root architecture check; invalid domain slice status and dangling producer edges are tested negatively, without a new domain registry or solver. Distribution legacy DS1=BLOCKED remains explicitly outside this gate until its owner evidence is qualified, not silently translated.
blockers: The formal issue census records evidence from its observed SourceCut; neither slice grants live runtime authority.
slices.nextAction: Keep owner-native source-identity and exact CDC tests; do not introduce new authorities.

slices.label: SourceBoundFormalIssueProvenance
acceptance: FORMAL-02 owner-local plan, census input and owners.toml must be regular source-tree files; symlink and traversal impersonation fail closed.
A valid owner-local plan passes without claiming domain correctness; recheck only on changed source or consumer assumptions.

For a named source-bound R2.1 Python consumer witness, an unconditional module-level pytest skip/xfail must fail the native AST evidence check even if the test function name exists; conditionally skipped integration tests never imply execution PASS.
blockers: The formal issue census records evidence from its observed SourceCut; neither slice grants live runtime authority.
slices.nextAction: Keep owner-native source-identity and exact CDC tests; do not introduce new authorities.
